source_title: Operating Aircraft or Unmanned Aircraft Carelessly, Negligently or Recklessly
regulated_activity: Careless, negligent, or reckless UAS operation endangering property, life, or limb
summary: Conn. Gen. Stat. § 15-72 prohibits operating any aircraft or unmanned aircraft carelessly, negligently, or recklessly, or in a manner endangering the property, life, or limb of any person, with regard to the proximity of other aircraft, weather conditions, field conditions, and the territory flown over. Originally applicable only to manned aircraft, P.A. 24-40 (effective July 1, 2024) amended the statute to expressly add unmanned aircraft. 'Careless, negligent or reckless operation' is defined by cross-reference at § 15-34(10).

source_title: Critical Infrastructure Facility UAS Flight and Surveillance Restriction
regulated_activity: Operating a UAS less than 250 ft above, or within 100 horizontal ft of, a defined 'critical infrastructure facility'; or using a UAS to surveil, gather evidence about, or collect information regarding such a facility without the owner/administrator's prior approval
requirement_type: Prohibition (Class A misdemeanor), with an authorized-worker exception
summary: Public Act 25-1, effective October 1, 2025, makes it an offense to operate a UAS less than 250 ft above, or within 100 horizontal ft of, a 'critical infrastructure facility' — defined to include electrical generation/substation/control facilities, petroleum/fuel storage and processing facilities, chemical/rubber manufacturing or storage facilities, correctional facilities, telecommunications infrastructure, commercial ports/harbors/rail yards/truck terminals, gas manufacturing/distribution plants, FCC-licensed broadcast transmission facilities, above-ground oil/gas/chemical pipelines, high/significant-hazard dams, air navigation facilities, military facilities, water/wastewater treatment and pumping infrastructure, defense-contractor facilities, government office buildings, hospitals, public-safety buildings, and state/locally owned bridges — and separately prohibits using a UAS to surveil, gather evidence about, or collect information regarding such a facility without prior approval from the owner or administrator. Violation is a Class A misdemeanor (up to nearly one year imprisonment, up to a $2,000 fine, or both). The act exempts law enforcement, government employees, military personnel, and contractors authorized to work in the area.

summary: Public Act 25-1 prohibits equipping any aircraft or UAS with a deadly weapon, dangerous instrument, firearm, ammunition, explosive, or incendiary device, effective October 1, 2025. source_title: Regulation of Commercial Unmanned Aircraft — Municipal Preemption
citation: Conn. Gen. Stat. § 7-149b (Public Act 17-52 / Senate Bill 975)
regulated_activity: Municipal ordinances or resolutions regulating the ownership, possession, purchase, sale, use, transportation, or operation of commercial UAS
summary: Conn. Gen. Stat. § 7-149b, enacted by Public Act 17-52 (Senate Bill 975), prohibits a municipality from enacting or enforcing an ordinance or resolution regulating the ownership, possession, purchase, sale, use, transportation, or operation of a commercial UAS, except as otherwise authorized by state or federal law and to the extent not in conflict with Connecticut Airport Authority policies and procedures. A municipality that is also a 'water company' as defined in the general statutes may enact and enforce ordinances regulating or prohibiting private and commercial UAS use or operation over that municipality's public water supply and Class I or Class II land, provided the ordinance does not conflict with federal law or Connecticut Airport Authority policy. Secondary sources describe the preemption as applying specifically to commercial UAS operation (i.e., FAA remote-pilot-certificate-based flights), leaving recreational/hobby flight open to local ordinance.
practical_interpretation_aec_expert: Use the statewide rule as the regulatory baseline, while separately screening site-control rules and any local authority preserved by the preemption provision. Record that jurisdictional check in the project flight-planning package.

source_title: Prohibition on Remote Controlled Aircraft or Drones on State Parks and Forests
uas_topic: State park / public land UAS restriction
regulated_activity: Operating a remote-controlled aircraft or drone on DEEP-controlled state parks, state forests, or other DEEP lands
requirement_type: Prohibition, except with a Commissioner-issued Special Use License
permit_or_approval_required: Yes — Special Use License from the DEEP Commissioner
summary: DEEP's Regulations of Connecticut State Agencies § 23-4-1(o) prohibits operating a remote-controlled aircraft or drone at Connecticut State Parks, State Forests, or other DEEP-controlled lands unless specifically authorized by the Commissioner in a Special Use License. DEEP's own published guidance states this applies to both recreational and commercial operators and cites public-safety (uncontrolled-descent risk from untrained pilots), noise (§ 23-4-1(x), prohibiting noise that infringes on other visitors' enjoyment), and wildlife-disturbance (§ 23-4-1(b)) rationales. DEEP's guidance further states that no public UAS use is authorized through its Special Use License application/process, implying the license path is not readily available to ordinary applicants.
